method.candidate_selection: Purposive secondary screen: varied Java domains, accessible pinned default-tip trees and enough observed two-parent history to justify limited path checks; not a random comparison.
method.commits_at_pin: Size of the GitHub commits endpoint listing reachable from pin (all parents within this ancestry, no other ref tips). per_page=1 final nonempty page and following empty page verified.
method.java_size: Count and sum of Git tree blob-entry sizes (.java suffix). Includes tests and vendored/generated Java where present; no LOC, token or runtime interpretation.
method.windows: First 25 REST API commits at pin, and first 25 at or before 2025-11-19T00:00:00Z / 2018-11-19T00:00:00Z within pin ancestry. Records are [merge-or-ordinary commit SHA,[all parent SHAs]].
method.overlaps: First two two-parent commits per window, or all if fewer, in API order. Compare p2...p1 and p1...p2, require same reported merge-base, intersect status=modified case-sensitive .java paths. At 300 returned files or a surfaced limit, observed intersections are lower bounds. Multiple merge-base ambiguity, renames and attributes are not resolved.
method.size_kib: GitHub live repository size snapshot (KiB), a rough relative transfer-cost signal. Extraction runtime, transfer bytes and memory have not been measured.
method.coverage: Metadata, pinned trees, bounded parent comparisons and isolated text probes. No production extraction, so no Parquet rows or class rates.

repositories.assessment: Release maintenance merges are frequent in the three windows. Five parent comparisons reach the API file cap; use local Git for a capped pilot.
Smallest repository-size snapshot of the five and overlaps in two periods; prioritize a bounded production pilot.
Two-parent merges in all windows, but the six probes found no bilateral modified Java path.
Game domain and four shared paths in one older merge; check repeated-merge weighting and packaged assets before transfer.

repositories.license: GPLv3 code; separate artwork and third-party terms
